response.chief_complaint_evolution: At triage (14:20), the patient presented with sharp chest pain following physical exertion (unloading maize sacks), exacerbated by pressing on the chest wall and twisting, without systemic or ischemic features (no SOB, sweating, or pain with walking). Referral letter (14:45) noted an otherwise unremarkable examination from a private clinic visit. At 15:10, the clinical officer confirmed the pain was fully reproducible on palpation of the costochondral area and managed it as a musculoskeletal complaint.

key_findings_timeline.finding: chest pain since yesterday after unloading maize sacks. sharp, worse on pressing chest wall and on twisting. no sweating, no SOB, pain not related to walking
pain fully reproducible on palpation of costochondral area, ECG normal sinus, trop not indicated

response.end_state_clinical_picture: Musculoskeletal chest pain (costochondritis/chest wall strain) confirmed by reproducible pain on costochondral palpation. Acute coronary syndrome / cardiac etiology ruled out clinically and via normal sinus rhythm on ECG. Patient reassured and prescribed NSAIDs.
response.pending_vs_confirmed: Confirmed: Normal sinus rhythm on ECG; costochondral tenderness/reproducible chest wall pain. Pending: None (Troponin was deemed not indicated and not ordered).
